sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: The strongest supported explanations are ad fatigue and broader campaign inefficiency: exposure frequency was higher as advertising response and attributed outcomes weakened. Overall sessions, orders, and conversion also declined, so the advertising pattern may be part of a wider change. The evidence does not establish a causal mechanism. Checkout failure, stockout, customer feedback, and delivery evidence do not establish explanations for the campaign deterioration.

sections.title: Observed evidence
sections.text:
Campaign performance versus baseline and peers: 5 campaign(s) analysed over 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z: CTR 0.40%, spend £623.29, 5 attributed orders, CPA £124.66, ROAS 0.95. Versus baseline: CTR -77.9%, hourly spend +26.7%, hourly attributed orders -81.5%. Observations are simulated ad-platform records; frequency and CTR describe exposure and response, not intent.

Revenue, orders and conversion versus baseline: Over 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z: 18 orders, net revenue £1943.82, 851 sessions, conversion 2.12%. Baseline (30 h): hourly revenue -53.8% change, hourly orders -53.8%, hourly sessions -37.8%. Decomposition: sessions share 0.616, conversion share 0.386, AOV share -0.002 of the revenue change. Values are simulated business records; this describes what changed, not why.

Sessions, conversion and checkout failures: 851 sessions and 18 orders over 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z (conversion 2.12%); 0 checkout failures (0.00% of sessions). Baseline: conversion 2.85% (-25.8% change), failures per hour n/a change, sessions per hour -37.8% change. Simulated storefront records; device and channel slices join orders to their canonical session.

Inventory levels, depletion and demand velocity: 17 product(s) observed to 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z: 0 at zero available units, 0 projected to run out within 72 h at current velocity, 5 units depleted in the 30 h window, 0 out-of-stock checkout failures. No product is currently out of stock. Simulated inventory records derived from canonical inventory.level_changed events.

Review volume, low ratings and delivery complaints: 3 reviews over 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z: 0 rated ≤2 (0.0%), average rating 4.00, 1 mention delivery terms. Most low-rated products: Nike Dunk Low Retro (0/2), Nike Mercurial Superfly 11 Academy (0/1). Simulated review records; delivery mentions are a keyword heuristic.

Delivery promise cohort and delayed orders: Cohort of 52 promises due in the 30 h ending 2026-10-05T12:00:00.000Z: 3 not delivered by promise (late rate 5.8%). Baseline late rate 7.1% on 14 promises (-19.2% change). 3 order(s) received a delayed status (average recorded delay 1556 min), 0 lost; 2 shipped order(s) are past promise with no delivered or lost event at the cutoff. Simulated fulfilment records; cohort membership is by promise due date, so immature promises never read as healthy.

sections.title: Competing explanations
sections.text:
ad fatigue (moderate): Higher average exposure frequency coincided with substantially lower click-through response and weaker attributed outcomes. This is consistent with ad fatigue, but the evidence does not establish that repeated exposure caused the decline or whether frequency rose before response weakened.

ad inefficiency (moderate): Spend continued while clicks, attributed sessions, and attributed orders weakened, supporting deteriorating campaign efficiency. The available evidence does not identify whether delivery, targeting, bidding, traffic composition, or another factor explains it.

unknown (weak): A measurement or attribution change remains possible but is not documented. The broader decline in sessions, orders, and conversion alongside weaker campaign results does not distinguish a measurement change from genuine deterioration or establish a single underlying cause.
